module_title: Major Parks, Flagship Species, and Conservation Projects
introduction: At this level, we memorize major National Parks state-wise and focus heavily on their 'Flagship Species'—the specific iconic animals for which these parks are globally famous.

core_concepts.title: National Parks of Assam
core_concepts.description: 'Kaziranga' is world-famous for the One-horned Rhinoceros. 'Manas' is known for the Wild Water Buffalo and the rare Pygmy Hog.

core_concepts.title: National Parks of Gujarat
core_concepts.description: 'Gir National Park' is the only natural habitat of the 'Asiatic Lion' in the entire world. Gujarat also hosts the 'Marine National Park' in the Gulf of Kutch.

core_concepts.title: National Parks of Rajasthan
core_concepts.description: 'Ranthambore' and 'Sariska' are famous Tiger reserves. 'Keoladeo Ghana' (in Bharatpur) is a paradise for migratory birds, notably the Siberian Crane.

core_concepts.title: Project Tiger (1973)
core_concepts.description: Launched by the Indira Gandhi government in 1973 to save the declining tiger population. Jim Corbett was the first Tiger Reserve to come under this project.

important_entities.name: Dachigam National Park
important_entities.significance: Located in Jammu & Kashmir, it is the only area where the Kashmir Stag, locally known as 'Hangul', is found.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common trap in MP state exams: 'Kanha' is the largest national park in Madhya Pradesh, but 'Bandhavgarh' National Park has the 'highest density' (most tigers per square kilometer) in the state.

exam_strategy_tips: Match the following questions are extremely common: Kaziranga -> Rhino, Gir -> Lion, Dachigam -> Hangul. Rote memorize these pairs.
Note that Keoladeo (Bharatpur) was formerly called a Bird Sanctuary but is now a National Park and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
